summary.text: 字 is traditionally analyzed as a child (子) beneath a roof (宀), with 子 also serving as a sound component. It commonly means “written character” today.

formation.text: The traditional account treats 字 as phonosemantic: 宀 depicts a roof or indoor setting, while 子 depicts the child and is assigned a sound role. This historical interpretation has been challenged, though the reported alternative is not detailed enough to assess.

components.text: In the traditional analysis, 宀 depicts the roof or indoor setting around the child; this graphic interpretation has been challenged, and the reported alternative is not specified.
子 depicts the child in the traditional scene and is also assigned a sound role.

history.text: A reported bronze-form account describes 子 beneath 宀. A catalog lists a Shang-period rubbing associated with 字父己觶, but the listing does not establish the inscription’s reading or make it the earliest attestation.
The traditional graphic analysis has been challenged, but the reported alternative is not detailed. The available evidence does not identify graphic corruption or miscopying.

uncertainties.text: The child-under-a-roof construction is a transmitted historical explanation; the reported disagreement is too limited to evaluate competing analyses.

senses.period: Han lexicographic account; earlier dating unresolved
senses.text: A Han lexicographic account gives birth or nurture as meanings but does not establish when they arose or whether they represent one original sense.
字 commonly means a written character; the earliest use of this sense is not dated here.
“Word” is also a recorded meaning, but its chronology and relation to birth or nurture are unresolved.

developments.text: A later commentary links birth to nurture and then to written characters; a distinct-root or derivation-from-producing account is also reported. The proposed relationship and its chronology remain unresolved.

limitations.text: The Han-era explanation that written forms multiply, and dictionary gloss lists, do not independently establish the chronology or development of these meanings.

overview.text: 字 is traditionally explained as a child (子) beneath a roof (宀), with 子 also supplying a sound cue. Today it commonly means “written character.”

components.text: In the traditional scene, the roof sets an indoor setting around the child.
子 is the child in the traditional scene and is also assigned a sound role.

takeaway.text: The old explanation links birth and nurture with written characters, but that development and its chronology remain unresolved.

relationships.text: In the traditional construction, 宀 depicts the roof or indoor setting in the proposed child-under-a-roof scene.
In the traditional construction, 子 depicts the child beneath the roof.

The traditional account assigns 子 a sound role. Exact Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese entries reported from a local TSV have compatible consonant correspondences, but their exact rows were not independently checked against the public dataset; they do not alone prove the graphic analysis. Modern Mandarin 子 zǐ and 字 zì are comparable but do not establish the ancient relation.
